text: {"rules":[{"id":"HIV-SCREEN-ADOL-15-21","version":"2025","title":"Adolescent HIV screening at least once between ages 15 and 21 (Bright Futures footnote 30)","source_quote":"Screen adolescents for HIV at least once between the ages of 15 and 21","grade":"not graded (Bright Futures/AAP periodicity schedule footnote)","effective_date":"2025-02","action":"Confirm at least one HIV screening test was performed between ages 15 and 21","denominator":"{\"age\": {\"min\": 21, \"max\": 21, \"at\": \"end\"}, \"quote\": \"between the ages of 15 and 21\", \"derived\": {\"min\": \"evaluated at age 21, when the 15-21 screening window closes, so patients still inside the window are not counted as missed\", \"max\": \"same as min: only the cohort whose window closes this measurement year\"}}","numerator":"{\"immunization_placeholder_removed\": null}","exclusions":"[]"}],"coverage_notes":["CORRECTION for rule HIV-SCREEN-ADOL-15-21: the numerator field must be read as {\"procedure\": {\"concept\": \"hiv_test\", \"window\": [\"{MY-6}-01-01\", \"{MY}-12-31\"]}, \"quote\": \"at least once between the ages of 15 and 21\", \"derived\": {\"window\": \"a patient aged 21 at end of MY turned 15 during MY-6; the calendar-year window approximates ages 15-21 because the grammar has no birth-date-relative windows\"}}. hiv_test is a lab test, encoded with the procedure type because the grammar has no lab-order type; this rule needs human review before use.","Rule HIV-SCREEN-ADOL-15-21 is derived and approximate: the source ages 15-21 are birth-date-relative, but the grammar only supports measurement-year-relative windows, so the window may include a test done shortly before the 15th birthday or miss one done at age 21 in a later year.","Footnote 30 also says youth at increased risk of HIV should be retested annually or more frequently after initial screening. This depends on risk assessment (uncomputable: HIV exposure risk / sexual and drug-use history) and was not represented as a rule.","Footnote 32, HCV screening at least once between ages 18 and 79, was not encoded. The once-per-lifetime window spans 61 years, which cannot be expressed without birth-relative windows. It restates the USPSTF/CDC recommendation, so it is better captured from that source. Annual reassessment for people at increased risk, such as past or current injection drug use, is uncomputable because it needs exposure history.","Footnote 14 (behavioral and social-emotional screening, family-centered, social determinants) was not represented. It only points to external guidance and gives no ages or interval on this page.","Footnote 15 (CRAFFT substance-use assessment; consider naloxone if there is concern) was not represented. It names a tool and a clinician-judgment action, with no ages or interval stated here.","Footnote 16 (screen adolescents for depression and suicide risk) was not represented. The ages and interval are defined in the periodicity table, not in this footnote text.","Footnote 17 (age-appropriate physical exam at each visit) was not represented. It is visit content and is not separately checkable.","Footnote 18 (schedules may be modified by entry point and individual need) is catch-up/individualization logic and was not represented.","Footnotes 19-21 (confirm newborn metabolic, hearing and bilirubin screening was done, verify results, follow up) were not represented. They are result-verification and follow-up actions with no computable timing given here.","Footnote 22 (pulse oximetry CCHD screening after 24 hours of age, before hospital discharge) was not represented. It is an inpatient newborn procedure tied to discharge timing, outside clinic EHR data, and there is no concept for it in the vocabulary.","Footnote 23 (immunization schedules per AAP COID/Red Book) was not represented. The schedules are external.","Footnote 24 (iron/anemia risk assessment or screening) was not represented. It depends on risk assessment and an external policy.","Footnote 25 (lead exposure risk) was not represented. It depends on lead exposure risk, which is uncomputable.","Footnote 26 (universal screening requirements for Medicaid patients or high-prevalence areas) was not represented. Payer and geographic prevalence conditions are not reliably available.","Footnote 27 (TB testing on recognition of high-risk factors) was not represented. It depends on risk factors, which are uncomputable.","Footnote 28 (cardiovascular health guidelines reference) was not represented. It is a reference only.","Footnote 29 (adolescent STI screening per Red Book) was not represented. The criteria are external and depend on sexual history.","Footnote 31 (HBV risk assessment per USPSTF/Red Book) was not represented. It depends on risk assessment.","Footnote 33 (sudden death in the young risk assessment) was not represented. It depends on family history and symptoms, which are uncomputable.","Footnote 34 (cervical cancer screening per USPSTF; pelvic exam indications before 21) was not represented. It refers to external guidance.","Footnotes 35-36 (dental home assessment, oral health risk assessment, referral, fluoride toothpaste) were not represented. Dental home status is not reliably structured, and the ages are in the periodicity table.","Footnote 37 (fluoride varnish starting at primary tooth eruption, every 3 to 6 months based on caries risk) was not represented. The start depends on tooth eruption and the interval depends on caries risk, both uncomputable.","Footnote 38 (consider oral fluoride supplementation if the water source is deficient) was not represented. It depends on water fluoride status and clinician judgment."]}
